transcript.text: dishwaher leakin water all over the floor and the plug sockets are right next to it whats going on

This is an immediate electrical hazard. Water and electricity do not mix, and having a leaking dishwasher directly adjacent to live plug sockets creates a serious risk of electric shock or fire.

Here is exactly what you need to do right now, in order:

### 1. IMMEDIATE ACTION: Cut the Power
• Do NOT touch the dishwasher if it is plugged into a socket on the wall and water is pooling around that socket.
• Go to your main electrical fuse box/circuit breaker panel.
• Find the circuit that controls the kitchen or specifically the dishwasher (if labeled) and switch it OFF.
• If you cannot identify the specific circuit, switch off the main power to the house until a professional can help.

### 2. Do NOT Use Plug Sockets Near the Leak
• Assume all sockets near the water are live and dangerous until proven otherwise by an electrician.
• Do not plug or unplug anything in that area while the floor is wet.

### 3. Stop the Water Source
• Once the power is safely cut, you can turn off the water supply valve to the dishwasher (usually located under the sink or behind the appliance).
• If there is no visible valve, stop using any taps in the kitchen and consider turning off the main water supply if the leak is severe.

### 4. Assess the Situation
There are two likely scenarios:
• Scenario A: The dishwasher itself is leaking. This could be due to a failed hose, pump seal, or door gasket. Even after fixing this, you must ensure no water has entered the electrical socket.
• Scenario B: Water is coming from elsewhere (e.g., sink) and hitting the socket. If the leak isn’t from the dishwasher but from a pipe under the sink, the socket may already be compromised by moisture ingress.

### 5. Call Professionals
• Call a qualified electrician immediately to inspect the plug sockets and wiring near the leak. They need to check for:
• Moisture inside the socket outlets.
• Short circuits or damaged insulation.
• Whether the sockets are properly rated for kitchen environments (IP-rated).
• Call a dishwasher repair technician once the electrical safety is confirmed, to fix the source of the leak.

### Why This Is Dangerous
• Electric Shock: Water conducts electricity. If it enters an open or faulty socket, it can travel through metal pipes, appliances, or even the floor, creating a shock hazard anywhere in the kitchen.
• Fire Risk: A short circuit caused by water can generate heat and sparks, potentially igniting nearby materials.

Summary: Turn off the power at the breaker NOW. Do not touch anything electrical near the water. Call an electrician before doing anything else.

DO NOT touch the socket or the dishwasher. You are in immediate danger of electric shock.

Here is exactly what you must do, RIGHT NOW:

### 1. Go to your fuse box / circuit breaker panel IMMEDIATELY.
• Do not try to unplug it from the wall if the water is already near an extension lead or socket on the floor.
• Find the switch for the kitchen or the specific circuit for the dishwasher and flip it OFF.
• If you don’t know which one it is, switch off the MAIN power to your house.

### 2. Do NOT touch anything wet.
• Keep your feet dry. Stand on a dry surface (like a wooden floor, not a rug if it’s damp underneath).
• Do not step in the water if you can avoid it.

### 3. Once the power is OFF at the fuse box:
• You can now safely approach the area.
• Turn off the water supply to the dishwasher (usually under the sink or behind the appliance).
• Unplug the extension lead and any other appliances from the affected sockets only after you are sure the main power is cut.

### 4. After this:
• Call a qualified electrician immediately to check the socket and wiring for water damage. Water in an electrical socket can cause short circuits, fires, or lethal shocks even after the leak stops.
• Call a dishwasher repair technician once the area is safe and dry.

Summary: Your only safe option right now is to cut the power at the fuse box. Do not touch the wall sockets.
ok going to the fuse box now. its an indesit one and the housemate put fairy washing up liquid in cos we ran out of tablets, theres suds everywhere. should i just switch the whole house off?

Yes, switch off the main power immediately. Do not waste time trying to find the specific circuit for the dishwasher. The situation is critical because:

1.  Water + Electricity = Lethal Risk: Water conducts electricity. If it’s touching an extension lead or a wall socket, you could be electrocuted if you touch anything connected to that power while standing on wet floors.
2.  Fairy Liquid is Conductive: Dish soap creates soapy water, which is even more conductive than plain water. This increases the risk of short circuits and electric shock significantly.
3.  Suds are Spreading: The bubbles indicate active leaking and movement of water toward electrical sources.

Steps to take RIGHT NOW:

1.  Go straight to your fuse box.
2.  Switch off the MAIN switch (usually a large red or black switch at the top). If there isn’t one, turn off all individual circuit breakers.
3.  Do not touch any sockets, plugs, or the dishwasher itself until you are certain the power is completely off.
4.  Once power is cut:
• Turn off the water supply to the dishwasher (usually under the sink).
• Do NOT try to drain the machine yourself if it means standing in water near electrical points.
5.  Call a professional:
• An electrician must inspect all sockets and wiring that were exposed to soapy water. Soapy residue can cause corrosion and short circuits even after drying.
• A dishwasher technician will need to clean out the suds and check for damage caused by the detergent misuse.

Do not use any electrical appliances in the kitchen until an electrician has confirmed it is safe.
